statement: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^2e^x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
solution:
Integrate by parts with $u=x^2$, $dv=e^x\,dx$ (so $du=2x\,dx$, $v=e^x$):
$$\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int 2xe^x\,dx.$$
For $\int 2xe^x\,dx$, integrate by parts again: $u=2x$, $dv=e^x\,dx$, giving $2xe^x-\int 2e^x\,dx=2xe^x-2e^x$. Hence
$$\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x.$$
Evaluating from $0$ to $1$:
$$\left[e^x(x^2-2x+2)\right]_0^1 = e(1-2+2)-2(1)=e-2.$$
